sections.label: Added
items: Backup & restore: a new Global panel with Export and Import buttons. Export downloads a JSON file of all your rules and settings; Import loads one on another device or after a reinstall (it replaces the current settings, then reloads).
Since settings are stored per-browser-profile and don't sync across devices, this is the supported way to move them — the Help page documents the process.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Fixed "kQuotaBytesPerItem quota exceeded" errors that silently dropped saves (e.g. after copying rules). Settings now live in chrome.storage.local, which has a multi-megabyte budget and no 8KB-per-item cap, instead of chrome.storage.sync.
Existing settings are migrated automatically on first load, so no rules are lost. (Trade-off: settings no longer sync across devices via Chrome sign-in.)

sections.label: Changed
items: Labelled Snooze as Experimental.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Dragging an "add element" button into the mock-up bar now actually adds the element. The drop was being silently rejected by a drag-effect mismatch (the button offered "copy" while the zone expected "move"), so it looked right but never stuck.

sections.label: Added
items: Copy Rule: a Copy button next to Delete duplicates a rule (with its own fresh IDs), drops it right below the original, and jumps to it.
Deleting a rule now asks for confirmation (Cancel / Confirm Delete) to prevent accidental loss.
Adding a rule now scrolls to and expands the new rule, so it's obvious one was created even when the list is long.
You can add a bar-text element by dragging its button straight into a Left/Center/Right zone of the mock-up bar (in addition to clicking it).

sections.label: Fixed
items: The toolbar popup no longer offers "Create rule for this page" when a rule already covers the page — the button becomes "Edit rule for this page" and opens that rule.
Font size is now validated like bar height: a value above 120 is rejected instead of silently persisting.
Adding the first element to a rule with no elements now adds only the element you picked, instead of also creating a stray Text element.

sections.label: Removed
items: Removed the Fleet Server Info API token field — the public /version endpoint is used and needs no token.

sections.label: Changed
items: Bar Text: removed the per-segment Justification dropdown. Placement is set entirely by dragging a segment into the Left/Center/Right zone of the mock-up bar.
Each segment's main field (Text, or Display Template) now sits beside its Label where the Justification dropdown used to be, saving vertical space.

sections.label: Added
items: Remove a segment by dragging its chip out of the mock-up bar and releasing (the chip turns red to confirm). The segment's Delete button still works too.

sections.label: Fixed
items: The rule Preview now reflects Blur: the pinned preview bar frosts the settings content that scrolls behind it, matching how the real bar blurs the page, so you can judge the blur amount while editing.

sections.label: Changed
items: Blur now maxes out at 20px (was 50). Backdrop blur becomes mushy well before 50, so the range is now the practical frosted-glass span.

sections.label: Changed
items: Font Style and Font Weight are now a single Font Style dropdown: Normal, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic. (The granular numeric weight is gone; existing rules map automatically — 600+ reads as Bold.)
Font Size now goes up to 120px (was 32) to match the maximum bar height; font size is still capped to the bar height on the page.
The "Prepend GitHub issue/PR number" toggle now only appears on rules that target github.com, and has more breathing room above it.

sections.label: Changed
items: Tab indicator is now labelled Experimental: it can't work on every site. Some sites (e.g. GitHub, NYTimes) continually rewrite their own favicon, which overrides the indicator; it's reliable on sites with a static favicon (e.g. Fleet servers, Google).

sections.label: Removed
items: Removed the global Domain blocklist. Per-domain exclusions will return later as a per-rule option (so you can exclude specific pages/sections of a domain while a rule still applies to the rest), which is the more useful shape.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Tab Title no longer flickers back to the plain title shortly after a GitHub issue/PR tab loads (then only re-prepending when you click the tab). GitHub swaps out the whole <title> element during hydration, which orphaned our title watcher; we now watch the <head> so the rename survives the swap and stays applied.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Tab Title (and the Page Title bar segment) now work on a full page load, not just after an in-page navigation. The page's real title is captured when the title observer connects, so on a freshly-opened GitHub issue tab the issue number is actually prepended (e.g. "#50648 …") instead of showing the plain title.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Tab Title GitHub prefix no longer replaces the whole tab title with the issue number twice (e.g. "#50764 #50764"). The real title is preserved, so it now reads "#50764 Fix the login bug" — focused or not, and after a reload.

Root cause: the browser trims trailing whitespace when reading document.title back, which slipped a title we'd written past our own loop guard and let it stack on itself. The guard now compares the normalized value, the prefix is only applied once the real title is known, and any already-doubled prefix self-heals.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Tab Title GitHub prefix no longer doubles the issue number (e.g. "#48222 - #48222 - …"); it's now idempotent.
The GitHub issue number is separated from the title by a single space instead of " - " to save tab space (e.g. "#12345 Fix the login bug").

sections.label: Fixed
items: No more "Extension context invalidated" errors after reloading/updating the extension: an orphaned content script now detects the dead context and stops its timers and observers instead of throwing.

sections.label: Changed
items: Fleet Role for team-scoped accounts (no global role) now shows the strongest team role held (e.g. Maintainer) instead of "Various".

sections.label: Changed
items: Fleet Role now shows the global role (e.g. Admin) when the account has one, even if it also has team roles — instead of "Various". Team-role logic still applies to accounts with no global role.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Fleet Role segment now actually shows the role: it authenticates the /me request with the session token from Fleet's cookie (the server requires the Authorization header, which the cookie alone didn't provide).

sections.label: Added
items: Sticky Header bar segment: shows the text of a page element matched by a CSS selector (default: GitHub's sticky issue/PR title), updating live as the page changes. Unlike Page Title (which reads document.title), this captures a site's own sticky-header text and can be pointed at any element/site.

sections.label: Added
items: Rule preview: tick Preview on a rule to pin a live preview of its bar to the top of the settings page. Only one at a time; it's temporary and resets when you leave settings.
Dynamic segments (Fleet/Browser/Page Title) show their template as a placeholder in the preview; real values appear on the actual page.

sections.label: Added
items: Fleet Role bar segment: shows the logged-in Fleet user's role (Admin, Maintainer, Observer+, etc.), read from the Fleet server's /me endpoint using your existing session. Shows only when signed in to a Fleet server.

sections.label: Added
items: Per-rule Tab Title: rename the browser tab on matching pages (prepend, append, or overwrite).
Prepend/append revert to the page's real title when the tab is focused (so the true title is a click away); overwrite persists, with a warning.
GitHub option: prepend the issue/PR number (e.g. "#1234 ") on GitHub issue/PR pages; persists on focus and never alters the page.
A Page Title segment reading the real title still works alongside tab renaming.

sections.label: Added
items: Page Title bar segment: shows the page's title ({title}) and updates as it changes — useful when a site's sticky-header title is hidden behind the bar.

sections.label: Added
items: Click any text in the color bar to copy it to the clipboard (briefly shows "Copied"). Only the text is clickable; the rest of the bar stays click-through.

sections.label: Changed
items: Rule sections (Bar Appearance, Bar Text) are now collapsible and collapsed by default, keeping expanded rules shorter.
Moved the Text / Fleet Server Info / Browser Info buttons to the top of the Bar Text section (below the mock-up) and dropped the "Add" prefix.

sections.label: Changed
items: Removed the global Display toggle; the in-rule bar mock-up is always shown.
Removed the "Saved" toast — settings auto-save silently; validation errors are still shown.

sections.label: Added
items: Global Tab indicator toggle: replaces the tab's favicon with a solid rounded tile in the matched rule's color.
The indicator only appears on background (unfocused) tabs — the active tab keeps its real favicon, so the page you're viewing is never obscured.
Follows the rule color across in-app (SPA) navigations.
Optional scope: apply the indicator to all rules or only selected ones, set in one place in the Global panel (rules stay uncluttered).

sections.label: Fixed
items: Domain Pattern with Wildcards on now matches the host as typed. Previously it silently required a subdomain, so a pattern like qa.example.com/* never matched qa.example.com itself. Add a *. prefix to include subdomains.

sections.label: Added
items: Browser Info segment for the bar text, showing the current tab's browser, full version, platform, and architecture (placeholders {browser}, {version}, {major}, {platform}, {arch}); works like the Fleet Server Info segment but reads the browser with no network request. Full version/platform/arch come from User-Agent Client Hints.

sections.label: Added
items: Create a rule for the current page directly from the toolbar popup: name (auto-filled from the domain), bar text, and a color picked from your swatches.
Wildcards are on by default (matches the whole site); turn them off to flag only the exact page.
New rules inherit all other settings from your default style.
Conflict check: if a rule already covers the page, the popup offers to edit it instead of creating a duplicate.
Confirmation with a bar preview and a one-click Edit rule that opens Settings expanded on the new rule.

sections.label: Added
items: Blur option that frosts the page behind the bar (available only when Bar Opacity is below 1; remembers its value when re-enabled).
Text Opacity option for the bar text.

sections.label: Changed
items: Renamed Background Color to Bar Color and Built-in Font to Font.
Reordered the Bar Appearance fields into a cleaner grid.
The bar always pushes page content down; removed the Page Placement option (it still overlays as the page scrolls).
Removed the redundant Oblique font style (identical to Italic).

sections.label: Changed
items: The changelog now reads from a single changelog.json file; the changelog page and the generated CHANGELOG.md both come from it.

sections.label: Added
items: Dedicated Changelog page, reachable from both Settings and Help.
A subtle Changelog link in the footer of the Settings and Help pages.

sections.label: Changed
items: The Settings Help button is now a lozenge, matching the Back buttons.
Simplified the Settings footer to just the version and Changelog link, matching the Help page footer.

sections.label: Changed
items: Global settings are now collapsible panels (Snooze, Default style, Domain blocklist, Display), matching the Rules accordion.
Each Global panel shows its current state in the summary.
Fixed cramped spacing in the Global section to match the Rules section.

sections.label: Fixed
items: The Default-style color picker no longer clips inside its collapsible panel.

sections.label: Added
items: Themed toolbar popup with an All sites master switch and a This page switch for the current tab's rule.
Global settings: master enable/disable, timed Snooze (1 hour / until tomorrow), default style for new rules, and a domain blocklist.

sections.label: Changed
items: Disabling globally remembers each rule's state; re-enabling restores it.
Per-page and global toggles are reflected on the matching rule switches.
Moved the bar layout mock-up toggle from Appearance into the Global section.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Reserved the scrollbar gutter so the column no longer shifts when a rule is expanded.
Aligned the Help page header with the Settings page for a seamless transition.

sections.label: Fixed
items: Help page now respects the theme set in Settings.
Help page Back button works again (moved inline scripts to an external file for MV3 compatibility).

sections.label: Added
items: Drag a text segment into any zone, and drag to reorder within a zone.
Toggle to show or hide the bar layout mock-up inside rules.

sections.label: Changed
items: Segment placement is now Left / Center / Right (removed Justify).

sections.label: Fixed
items: Zone labels no longer jump when a segment is placed.
Auto theme now follows the operating system correctly.

sections.label: Added
items: Light / Dark / Auto themes and a Chrome-native settings restyle.
Custom color picker with saved swatches for the Background and Text colors.
Fleet Server Info segment showing the server's version and branch, with an optional API token.
Multiple text segments per rule with independent placement, plus a drag-and-drop mock-up.
Extension version shown in the Help section.

sections.label: Baseline
items: Per-rule top bar with Domain Pattern and URL Components matching.
Per-rule text, style, height, and placement; collapsible rule list and in-extension help.
